name: Hovercraft
description: A small two-seat hovercraft: it floats a hand's width over the ground on its skirt, a fan at the back pushes it, and it turns with the fan's vanes and its fin. It drives with a car's keys, but like a real one it turns nose-first and keeps sliding, slides down hills, pushes through a little hump on water and drags on grass.
comment: A vehicle preset (#728, #793): see sedan.json for the format. movementType hover is the Hover movement type (FMantleVehicleHover): no wheels, engine or gearbox. Its numbers are a real light hovercraft's (#381; the Neoteric 2-seat and others, feature-381-hovercraft-plan.md): 600 kg on a 400 x 220 cm hull is 669 Pa on the cushion, as the Neoteric's 670. Lift is four pads, Chaos Modular suspensions with no wheel under them (Epic's quickstart: a suspension without wheels acts like a hovercraft skirt), one at each of the layout's wheel points on the hull's underside. The layout's wheels are those four points and nothing else: the document needs a steered and a driven wheel (its reader's rule), so it lists them, and the definition (UMantleVehicleHoverDefinition) turns them into pads and drives none; they are never drawn. The pads stand at 0.8 of the hull's length and width (320 and 176 cm, validate.py). Each pushes from chassis.hovercraft.pads.travel (50 cm) below it, harder as it comes down, so it rests where its share of the weight is its stiffness times the compression: 600 kg on four pads at the 20 cm hover height (body.groundClearance; real light hovercraft clear 18-20 cm) is 1470 N each over 30 cm, and a spring rate unit is 222 N/m (Epic's constraint takes the rate x 25 once per position iteration, measured), so springRate is 22.07 (validate.py holds it within 1 percent). The fan pushes 800 N, about a seventh of the weight, as real light hovercraft do (thrust-to-weight 0.09-0.18; it is also about the steepest slope one climbs from a stop), from its pod behind the hull near the center of mass's height; its push falls off with speed to nothing at defaults.maxSpeed (26 m/s), so with the hull's drag it tops out near 61 km/h on smooth ground and water (validate.py solves it; real 56-64), slower on grass, and its reverse vanes push 60 percent of it backwards (the Neoteric's reverse thrust; S: a brake while it moves forward, which fades out as it stops, then reverse). Its vanes turn the push up to 45 degrees either way on A and D (the most a document allows; a real one's rudders swing 60 or more to turn at low speed, DiscoverHover); the fin's rudder (0.8 m^2, 20 degrees) turns it at speed. Nothing grips the ground, so the hover chassis damps its sideways slide and its spin only a little (0.3 and 1 per second, at most 1 m/s^2 and 90 degrees/s^2: a real one turns nose-first and keeps sliding the old way; the builder's Grip and a script's Vehicles:SetSlideAssist change it) while a pad touches the ground, and Space drops the skirt: a brake of 2 per second, at most 5 m/s^2, which also holds it parked and on a hill. The skirt is drawn 8 cm off the ground and 10 cm wider than the hull, the fan pod and the fin on the root; only the hull collides. engine, transmission, suspension, steering, brakes and tires are the document's and drive nothing (the definition has no wheels); the camera, mass, drag and maxSpeed are the hovercraft's own.
